topics.title: Mapping the Earth: projections and physical maps
topics.ncert_sections: The Complexity of Mapping the Earth

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why every map projection of the Earth shows some distortion.
Compare what the Mercator and Robinson projections preserve and distort.
Identify the landforms and water bodies shown by each colour on a physical map.

topics.title: The oceans of the blue planet
topics.ncert_sections: The Blue of the Blue Planet, the Oceans; Ocean currents; Ocean trenches

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how oceans cover the Earth, support life and regulate climate.
Explain how warm and cold ocean currents affect the climate of coastal areas.
Describe ocean trenches such as the Mariana Trench and how life survives there.

topics.title: Coral reefs and smaller water bodies
topics.ncert_sections: The Great Barrier Reef; Smaller water bodies and waterways

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why coral reefs such as the Great Barrier Reef matter and what threatens them.
Distinguish seas, gulfs, bays, straits and canals and their role in trade.

topics.title: Asia: Tibetan Plateau, Gobi, Steppes and Urals

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the formation and importance of the Tibetan Plateau, the 'Third Pole'.
Describe the Gobi Desert and the Eurasian Steppes and their role in nature.
Explain the importance of the Ural Mountains and the tundra and taiga around them.

topics.title: Europe and Africa: plains, the Alps, deserts and the Nile

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the European Plain and the Alps support agriculture, water supply and settlement.
Describe the Sahara Desert and the African savannah and how life adapts to them.
Explain the importance of the River Nile for people in Africa.

topics.title: The Americas: Andes, Amazon, Atacama and North American landforms

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Andes and the Amazon and why they are important for the planet.
Describe the Atacama Desert and the environmental problem it faces.
Describe the Colorado Plateau, the Rockies, the Appalachians and the Great Lakes.

topics.title: Australia, cold deserts and caring for the Earth
topics.ncert_sections: The Australian Continent; Before we move on

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Great Australian Desert, its wildlife and its people.
Recognise that deserts can be cold, with Antarctica as the largest desert on Earth.
Evaluate how human actions disturb natural features and why sustainable use is needed.
